\section*{Test sheet: the stem-axis rule on m, I, T, ɪ}
Candidates for the central-stem letters: m (its middle stem), I, T and ɪ, above and below.
The stem's midline comes from its straight edges (control points); in semibold italic m the middle stem has one straight edge, and the midline is that edge moved by the median half-width.
{\color{pre}Grey}: the designer's precomposed letter. {\color{now}Green}: the patched fonts now (designer, candidate or curated anchor).
In the italic styles, {\color{dec}blue}: the rule at the declared slant (12°, 11.5°) from the end of the stem's straight part; {\color{own}red}: the rule at the stem's own angle (the midline extended).
In regular and semibold the two are the same ({\color{own}red}, ``rule'').
Composed letters are base + CGJ + mark (HarfBuzz would otherwise substitute the precomposed glyph); capitals take the \verb|.cap| accents.
The overlays draw red last, so where only red shows the variants coincide; the columns show each one alone.
Numbers: composed minus precomposed, in units, the horizontal centre of the mark with the slant removed (positive: right of the precomposed accent).
